chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: The Tonight Show appearance paid by his own publishing company
summary: His band appeared on the Tonight Show, financed by his Indigo Music company, which he describes as a racket where networks avoid paying scale.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So that was when the man with the moving picture came in, and we did that and oh, we wound up, we made a whole bunch of transcriptions for the Navy, and we did the Tonight Show, and I was running around --
Wow, what happened with the Tonight Show band?
Well, they weren't --Clarke was working for me. He wasn't in -- he was working in my band. He wasn't working the Tonight Show band the whole time.
Yeah, but did they just dismiss the Tonight Show band to bring your band in, or were there two bands on the show?
Oh, yeah, the Tonight Show band was there until they brought us on, and we finished out the -- they've done that a few times. They did it with Harry James.
I didn't remember their having a whole other band on, just parts of a band.
Well, see, the way that's done is they don't pay for that.

It's usually paid for by a record company, and in my case I wanted to do it so mine was paid for by Indigo Music Incorporated, a music publishing firm which I owned. And this is what happens anytime -- a lot of times the groups that go on there, they're not paid by NBC. This is the biggest racket in the world. They get away with murder. They use every angle in the world to keep the overhead down, and they're making millions off of that program. But it was all right with me. I figured gee, things are going good. This is probably my last fling. Let's go out in style, you know, let's do the Tonight Show. So we set it up and it didn't cost much. What the heck, the scale wasn't too much, and we'd done all these other things, and the pot was -- I wasn't in it to make any money anyway. I was having a ball, a good time.
